claims.text: The dispute is filed by the driver (dispute.filed_by = DRIVER), and the fare ledger records that the money has already moved the other way: the 5.00 SGD fee was charged at 09:09:34 and then returned to the rider and recovered from the driver at 09:29:30, so payment_status is REFUNDED with refund_issued_sgd 5.00. POL-GEN-03 fixes what each outcome means against the filer: a ruling for the driver must move that same 5.00 SGD back to him, whereas NO_ACTION — the party-relative value — leaves the present state, with the rider reimbursed, standing. The driver, as filer, must therefore make out on this trip's own evidence that the charge should be restored, and the rider's submission is that the record before the Tribunal does not carry it.

The pickup was scheduled for 09:00 and the driver arrived at 09:02:40 — 160 seconds after the time he had undertaken to be there — and he concedes the lateness in his own 09:03:00 message ('Hi, sorry a bit late, I'm at Blk 108 now'). The rider does not press POL-NS-24 as a voiding ground: that clause voids a fee only where arrival is after the scheduled time plus 300 s, i.e. 09:05:00, and the derived deadline check records arrived_by_deadline = true. The rider's submission is the narrower one: the lateness the driver himself admits is the factual core of her objection, and nothing on this record explains it — the one artifact that could have carried a traffic explanation, EV-ADVIS-06058-01, is MISSING with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight_multiplier 0.0 and carries no payload at all.

The rider does not press POL-NS-23, and the Tribunal should not read her case as turning on it: the record carries two in-app chat messages from the driver, at 09:03:00 and 09:06:20, and a placed in-app call at 09:05:10 (unanswered, 30 s), all before the 09:09:30 cancellation, and the derived contact block records obligation_met = true from EV-CHAT-06058 at weight 1.0. On this record the driver met the contact obligation and the rider gains nothing by arguing otherwise; her submission is that the fee's restoration must still be justified on the trip's own facts, not assumed from the platform's label.

Nothing in the evidence observes the rider. The only trace on file is the driver's own device trace (EV-GPS-06058, source DRIVER_DEVICE) and it carries no rider track at all — rider_track is empty — so the record's 'rider not on board' line at 09:07:45 is the platform's own conclusion rather than an observation of the rider. If the Tribunal treats the rider's non-appearance as a fact the no-show charge needs and finds that this record cannot establish it, POL-GEN-26 sends the case to a human reviewer with the 5.00 SGD held rather than collected; on an account whose only support is the driver's word, holding the amount is the rider's alternative ask to NO_ACTION.

The rider's profile — rating, account age, lifetime trips, cancellation rate, prior disputes, prior no-show flags — may inform how closely her assertion is scrutinised, but it cannot decide this trip: POL-GEN-01 confines every one of those fields to context and permits no profile field to establish a fact about this trip or its outcome. The rider's objection is answered from this trip's record — the schedule she was given and the time the driver actually arrived — and not from her history.

claims.text: The no-show condition was satisfied on timing. The driver arrived at 09:02:40, after the 09:00 scheduled pickup, so under POL-NS-21 the 300-second free wait ran from the driver's arrival and expired at 09:07:40; the driver cancelled at 09:09:30, 110 seconds after the free wait expired. The driver therefore cancelled at a time when the policy permitted it.

Arrival at the pickup is corroborated to the standard the category's arrival test requires. The nearest driver fix sits 6.48 m from the pickup point, well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, and that fix reports 5 m horizontal accuracy, inside the 25 m accuracy filter; the arrival event at 09:02:40 is therefore GPS-corroborated and the free wait properly started.

The driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is satisfied, not breached. The driver sent two in-app chat messages (09:03:00 and 09:06:20) and placed an in-app call at 09:05:10, all before cancelling at 09:09:30, and the record marks obligation_met as true. The rider read both messages (09:03:46 and 09:06:27), so contact was delivered and received before the cancellation.

The rider's 'the driver was late' objection does not engage POL-NS-24. The scheduled pickup plus five minutes fixed the deadline at 09:05:00, and the GPS-corroborated arrival was 09:02:40, so the driver arrived by the deadline; the record marks arrived_by_deadline true. On that clause the rider may not cancel at no charge and no refund of the fee is due.

The driver's own first message ('sorry a bit late') does not defeat the fee. POL-NS-21 expressly contemplates a scheduled trip where the driver arrives after the scheduled time and starts the free wait from arrival, and the driver still beat the 09:05:00 deadline in POL-NS-24. Arriving after 09:00 was therefore a lateness the policy absorbs, not a breach, and the driver waited out the full free wait before cancelling.

The rider's only statement, 'The driver was late, so I should not pay anything', is contradicted by the record and by the rider's own conduct. The driver arrived at 09:02:40, the rider read both driver messages, and the rider did not answer the 09:05:10 in-app call or appear at the pickup through the expiry of the free wait and the further 110 seconds the driver waited. The uncontradicted evidence is of a rider no-show, not of driver lateness.

The consequence under POL-NS-22 is that the 5.00 SGD fee is charged to the rider and transferred to the driver as compensation for time and fuel. The fare ledger records exactly 5.00 SGD charged, matching the 5.00 SGD policy fee, so the ruling should be DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 5.00.

The 5.00 SGD was reversed at 09:29:30 only as an interim response to the rider's complaint, pending review, and no clause supports leaving it reversed: POL-NS-23 was met and POL-NS-24 was not engaged. Because NO_ACTION is party-relative and would leave the refund to the rider standing and the driver unpaid, the ruling must affirmatively move the 5.00 SGD back to the driver under POL-GEN-03's DRIVER_COMPENSATION.

The contested value is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD threshold, so the AI ruling is final at any confidence; neither profile carries a fraud flag (rider_profile.fraud_flags 0 and driver_profile.fraud_flags 0), so no 0.95 confidence bar applies, and POL-NS-26 makes the no-show ruling final. There is no basis to escalate this fee away from the AI.

POL-GEN-26 has no open question to escalate. Every fact POL-NS-21 to POL-NS-24 needs is established on this record — arrival time, free-wait expiry, cancellation time, the two messages and the placed call. The traffic advisory is MISSING (EV-ADVIS-06058-01, status MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) and carries no fact, so its absence cannot fill in any element the driver's case needs or supply a justification for the rider.

The rider's no_show_cancellations_30d is 4, which — counting this trip if its fee stands — is at or above the POL-NS-25 threshold of 3, so the rider's account should be flagged for review under that clause. That is a referral naming the clause; it does not change the money, but it confirms the no-show pattern the driver encountered on this trip.

ruling.explanation:
To the driver and the rider: the 5.00 SGD no-show fee stands and is owed to the driver.

ARRIVAL AND FREE WAIT (POL-NS-21). The pickup was scheduled for 09:00. The driver's GPS trace puts him at the pickup at 09:02:40 (nearest fix 6.48 m from the pickup point, reporting 5 m accuracy — inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius and the 25 m accuracy filter), which corroborates the trip record's arrival event. Because this was a scheduled trip and the driver arrived after the scheduled time, the 300-second free wait ran from 09:02:40 and expired at 09:07:40. The driver cancelled at 09:09:30, 110 seconds after the free wait expired. The no-show cancellation was therefore permitted, and the driver's own 'sorry a bit late' message does not defeat the fee: POL-NS-21 expressly starts the free wait at arrival in exactly this situation.

CONTACT OBLIGATION (POL-NS-23). Two in-app messages (09:03:00 and 09:06:20) and a placed in-app call (09:05:10, unanswered, 30 s), all before the 09:09:30 cancellation. The obligation is met and supplies the rider with no ground.

THE RIDER'S LATENESS OBJECTION (POL-NS-24). 'The driver was late, so I should not pay anything' does not engage the clause that voids a fee. POL-NS-24 voids only where the driver arrives after the scheduled time plus five minutes, i.e. after 09:05:00; the driver arrived at 09:02:40 (arrived_by_deadline = true). No full refund is due on this ground, and POL-NS-24's goodwill credit does not fire because the driver also made contact.

ESCALATION ARGUMENTS REJECTED (POL-GEN-26). The missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-06058-01, status MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) carries no fact and is not needed — no rule in this category requires a traffic justification for the fee. The rider's further point that no artifact observes her directly (the only trace is the driver's own, with an empty rider_track) does not make the no-show undecidable: POL-NS-21's free-wait mechanism and the platform's own records are what the clauses read, and the record shows the free wait expiring with the rider not on board. There is no fact this record cannot establish, so no escalation.

WHO DECIDES. The contested value is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band; neither profile carries a fraud flag (rider_profile.fraud_flags 0, driver_profile.fraud_flags 0) and there is no safety flag (POL-GEN-21). Under POL-NS-26 the AI ruling on a no-show is final. Profiles were not used to decide the trip (POL-GEN-01).

OUTCOME. The fare ledger records exactly 5.00 SGD charged, matching the 5.00 SGD policy fee, so POL-NS-22 applies: the fee is transferred to the driver as compensation and the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 5.00. Because the driver filed, this moves the same 5.00 SGD — already refunded to the rider and recovered from the driver at 09:29:30 (fee_reversed) — back to the driver; the rider keeps no part of it. The rider's account is separately referred under POL-NS-25; that referral does not change the money.
referrals: POL-NS-25: flag the rider's account for review — rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d is 4, at or above the threshold of 3 counting this trip whose fee stands; mandatory upfront payment and temporary suspension pending Trust & Safety review.

You arrived at 09:02:40 (EV-TRIP-06058), after the 09:00 scheduled pickup, so under POL-NS-21 the 300-second free wait ran from your arrival and expired at 09:07:40; you cancelled at 09:09:30, 110 seconds after expiry. Arrival is GPS-corroborated — the nearest fix sits 6.48 m from the pickup, inside the 50 m STANDARD radius, reporting 5 m accuracy inside the 25 m filter (EV-GPS-06058). You met POL-NS-23's contact obligation: two in-app messages (09:03:00 and 09:06:20) and a placed call (09:05:10), all before the 09:09:30 cancellation, and the rider read both messages. POL-NS-24 is not engaged: you arrived by its deadline of 09:05:00 (scheduled 09:00 plus 5 minutes). The 5.00 SGD charged matches the 5.00 SGD policy fee, so POL-NS-22 gives DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00 SGD and POL-GEN-03 fixes amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd at that same figure. To the rider: your objection that the driver was late does not void the fee. He arrived at 09:02:40 — after your 09:00 scheduled pickup but before the 09:05:00 deadline POL-NS-24 sets — and POL-NS-21 expressly contemplates a scheduled trip where the driver arrives after the scheduled time, starting the free wait from arrival. No clause makes the lateness the driver himself admits ('sorry a bit late' at 09:03:00) a ground to keep the money, and the missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-06058-01, weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) carries no fact and was needed by no rule. Your alternative ask under POL-GEN-26 fails: every fact the no-show rules need — arrival time, free-wait expiry, cancellation time, the messages and the call before cancelling — is established on this record, and your non-appearance is recorded by the platform (wait timer expired at 09:07:45 with you not on board, after you read both messages and did not answer the call), not left to inference from the driver's trace alone. Your point that profiles are context only under POL-GEN-01 is correct and has been applied: nothing in either profile decides this trip. POL-NS-25 adds the referral above; it does not change the money. Confidence is 0.95 because every artifact carrying a deciding fact — trip record, GPS trace, chat log and fare ledger — has weight 1.0, and nothing caps the finding lower.

ruling.explanation:
Driver D-10671 filed this dispute. The fare ledger (EV-FARE-06058) records the 5.00 SGD no-show fee charged at 09:09:34 and then returned to rider R-80737 and withheld from the driver at 09:29:30 as an interim reversal after the rider's complaint. Because the driver is the filing party, the question is whether that 5.00 SGD should be restored to him, and on this record it should.

The no-show was valid. The pickup was scheduled for 09:00 and the driver arrived at 09:02:40. Under POL-NS-21, because he arrived after the scheduled time, the 300-second free wait ran from his arrival and expired at 09:07:40; he cancelled at 09:09:30, 110 seconds later — exactly what POL-NS-21 permits. The arrival is GPS-corroborated (EV-GPS-06058: nearest fix 6.48 m from the pickup, inside the 50 m STANDARD radius, reported at 5 m accuracy inside the 25 m filter).

The rider's grounds for refusing to pay do not hold. POL-NS-24 (driver no-show) is not engaged: the deadline was 09:05:00 and the driver arrived at 09:02:40, so the rider may not cancel at no charge and no full refund is due. The driver's lateness is real and he concedes it in his own 09:03:00 message ('Hi, sorry a bit late'), but POL-NS-21 expressly contemplates a scheduled trip where the driver arrives after the scheduled time and starts the free wait from arrival; arriving after 09:00 was therefore a lateness the policy absorbs, and the rider's 'the driver was late, so I should not pay anything' is answered by the schedule she was given and the time he actually arrived, not by her history (POL-GEN-01). POL-NS-23 (contact obligation) is satisfied, not breached: two in-app messages (09:03:00 and 09:06:20) and a placed in-app call (09:05:10), all before the 09:09:30 cancellation, with both messages read by the rider.

The rider's alternative ask for a human reviewer is refused. No clause makes the rider's physical presence a fact the charge must establish, and nothing requires the trace to carry a rider track; the no-show determination rests on the expired free wait and the cancellation, both established on the record. The one missing artifact, the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-06058-01 (status MISSING, weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT), carries no fact and no rule needs it, so POL-GEN-26 raises no open question here.

Under POL-NS-22 the fee therefore stands, and because the money has already moved the ruling restores it to the driver: DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 5.00. The fee charged is exactly the 5.00 SGD policy fee, so no POL-NS-22 fee-amount referral arises, and the driver met the deadline and the contact obligation, so no POL-NS-24 goodwill credit arises. The rider's no_show_cancellations_30d of 4 triggers the POL-NS-25 account review set out in the referrals. Confidence is 0.9, capped by the 1.0 weight_multiplier shared by the trip record, GPS trace, chat log and fare ledger that carry the deciding facts; at 5.00 SGD the dispute is below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, neither profile carries a fraud flag, and POL-NS-26 makes the AI ruling final.
referrals: POL-NS-25: flag rider R-80737's account for review — no_show_cancellations_30d is 4, at or above the threshold of 3 (counting this trip if its fee stands), so mandatory upfront payment and temporary suspension pending Trust & Safety review.

ruling.explanation: Both submissions have been weighed against the NO_SHOW_CHARGE policy. To the driver: your claim succeeds. The record shows you arrived at the pickup at 09:02:40 — after the 09:00 scheduled pickup — so under POL-NS-21 the 300-second free wait ran from your arrival and expired at 09:07:40; you cancelled at 09:09:30, 110 seconds after it expired, so the no-show condition is met. Your arrival is GPS-corroborated to the category's arrival test (EV-GPS-06058: nearest fix 6.48 m from the pickup, accuracy 5 m, inside the 50 m STANDARD radius and the 25 m filter), you met the POL-NS-23 contact obligation (two in-app messages at 09:03:00 and 09:06:20, and an in-app call at 09:05:10, all before the cancellation), and the 5.00 SGD charged matches the 5.00 SGD policy fee (POL-NS-22). Because that 5.00 SGD was reversed to the rider and recovered from you at 09:29:30 as an interim measure, the ruling moves the same 5.00 SGD back to you: DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 5.00. To the rider: your objections do not defeat the fee. The lateness the driver admits does not engage POL-NS-24, which voids the fee only if the driver arrives after the scheduled time plus 5 minutes (09:05:00); he arrived at 09:02:40, before that deadline (arrived_by_deadline = true), and he attempted contact, so neither a FULL_REFUND nor the POL-NS-24 5.00 SGD goodwill credit arises, and the missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-06058-01, MISSING, weight 0.0) carries no fact and justifies nothing. Nor does the absence of any observation of you create the open question POL-GEN-26 needs: the policy's test for the fee is the free wait plus a cancellation after it (POL-NS-21, POL-NS-22), not independent observation of the rider. Your profile fields (rating, account age, lifetime trips and the rest) are context only under POL-GEN-01 and decide nothing. Confidence: the contested value is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD band, so the AI ruling is final at any confidence and POL-NS-26 makes it final; neither profile carries a fraud flag, and the deciding facts rest on complete weight-1.0 artifacts (trip record and GPS trace for arrival and timing, chat log for contact, fare ledger for the 5.00 SGD fee). A clause-mandated referral follows: POL-NS-25, the rider's repeat no-show flag.

This does not change the money on this trip.

POL-GEN-03 fixes what each outcome means against the filer: a ruling for the driver must move that same 5.00 SGD back to him, whereas NO_ACTION — the party-relative value — leaves the present state, with the rider reimbursed, standing. The driver, as filer, must therefore make out on this trip's own evidence that the charge should be restored, and the rider's submission is that the record before the Tribunal does not carry it.

The pickup was scheduled for 09:00 and the driver arrived at 09:02:40 — 160 seconds after the time he had undertaken to be there — and he concedes the lateness in his own 09:03:00 message ('Hi, sorry a bit late, I'm at Blk 108 now'). The rider does not press POL-NS-24 as a voiding ground: that clause voids a fee only where arrival is after the scheduled time plus 300 s, i.e. 09:05:00, and the derived deadline check records arrived_by_deadline = true. The rider's submission is the narrower one: the lateness the driver himself admits is the factual core of her objection, and nothing on this record explains it — the one artifact that could have carried a traffic explanation, EV-ADVIS-06058-01, is MISSING with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight_multiplier 0.0 and carries no payload at all.

On this record the driver met the contact obligation and the rider gains nothing by arguing otherwise; her submission is that the fee's restoration must still be justified on the trip's own facts, not assumed from the platform's label.

Nothing in the evidence observes the rider. The only trace on file is the driver's own device trace (EV-GPS-06058, source DRIVER_DEVICE) and it carries no rider track at all — rider_track is empty — so the record's 'rider not on board' line at 09:07:45 is the platform's own conclusion rather than an observation of the rider. ledger.claim: The no-show condition was satisfied on timing. The driver arrived at 09:02:40, after the 09:00 scheduled pickup, so under POL-NS-21 the 300-second free wait ran from the driver's arrival and expired at 09:07:40; the driver cancelled at 09:09:30, 110 seconds after the free wait expired. The driver therefore cancelled at a time when the policy permitted it.

Arrival at the pickup is corroborated to the standard the category's arrival test requires. The nearest driver fix sits 6.48 m from the pickup point, well inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, and that fix reports 5 m horizontal accuracy, inside the 25 m accuracy filter; the arrival event at 09:02:40 is therefore GPS-corroborated and the free wait properly started.

The driver's contact obligation under POL-NS-23 is satisfied, not breached. The driver sent two in-app chat messages (09:03:00 and 09:06:20) and placed an in-app call at 09:05:10, all before cancelling at 09:09:30, and the record marks obligation_met as true. The rider read both messages (09:03:46 and 09:06:27), so contact was delivered and received before the cancellation.

The rider's 'the driver was late' objection does not engage POL-NS-24. The scheduled pickup plus five minutes fixed the deadline at 09:05:00, and the GPS-corroborated arrival was 09:02:40, so the driver arrived by the deadline; the record marks arrived_by_deadline true. On that clause the rider may not cancel at no charge and no refund of the fee is due.

The driver's own first message ('sorry a bit late') does not defeat the fee. POL-NS-21 expressly contemplates a scheduled trip where the driver arrives after the scheduled time and starts the free wait from arrival, and the driver still beat the 09:05:00 deadline in POL-NS-24. Arriving after 09:00 was therefore a lateness the policy absorbs, not a breach, and the driver waited out the full free wait before cancelling.

The rider's only statement, 'The driver was late, so I should not pay anything', is contradicted by the record and by the rider's own conduct. The driver arrived at 09:02:40, the rider read both driver messages, and the rider did not answer the 09:05:10 in-app call or appear at the pickup through the expiry of the free wait and the further 110 seconds the driver waited. The uncontradicted evidence is of a rider no-show, not of driver lateness.

The consequence under POL-NS-22 is that the 5.00 SGD fee is charged to the rider and transferred to the driver as compensation for time and fuel. The fare ledger records exactly 5.00 SGD charged, matching the 5.00 SGD policy fee, so the ruling should be DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 5.00.

The 5.00 SGD was reversed at 09:29:30 only as an interim response to the rider's complaint, pending review, and no clause supports leaving it reversed: POL-NS-23 was met and POL-NS-24 was not engaged. Because NO_ACTION is party-relative and would leave the refund to the rider standing and the driver unpaid, the ruling must affirmatively move the 5.00 SGD back to the driver under POL-GEN-03's DRIVER_COMPENSATION.

The contested value is 5.00 SGD, below POL-GEN-22's 10.00 SGD threshold, so the AI ruling is final at any confidence; neither profile carries a fraud flag (rider_profile.fraud_flags 0 and driver_profile.fraud_flags 0), so no 0.95 confidence bar applies, and POL-NS-26 makes the no-show ruling final. There is no basis to escalate this fee away from the AI.

POL-GEN-26 has no open question to escalate. Every fact POL-NS-21 to POL-NS-24 needs is established on this record — arrival time, free-wait expiry, cancellation time, the two messages and the placed call. The traffic advisory is MISSING (EV-ADVIS-06058-01, status MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT) and carries no fact, so its absence cannot fill in any element the driver's case needs or supply a justification for the rider.

The rider's no_show_cancellations_30d is 4, which — counting this trip if its fee stands — is at or above the POL-NS-25 threshold of 3, so the rider's account should be flagged for review under that clause. That is a referral naming the clause; it does not change the money, but it confirms the no-show pattern the driver encountered on this trip.
